statement_en: Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set for which there exists some $\epsilon>0$ such that in any subset of $A$ of size $n$ there is a subset of size at least $\epsilon n$ which contains no three-term arithmetic progression. Is it true that $A$ is the union of a finite number of sets which contain no three-term arithmetic progression?
statement_lean:
def HasFew3APs (A : Set ℕ) := ∃ (ε : ℝ), ε > 0 ∧ ∀ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ A → Finite B →
  ∃ (C : Set ℕ), C ⊆ B ∧ C.ncard ≥ ε * B.ncard ∧ ThreeAPFree C

theorem erdos_54005 :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Infinite A → HasFew3APs A →
    ∃ n, ∃ (S : Fin n → Set ℕ), (∀ i, ThreeAPFree (S i)) ∧ A = ⋃ i : Fin n, S i := by
  sorry
